Part 1 · Scenarios

Which events can overpressure K-100, and which one governs each valve?

Part 1 · the plan

From the pressure systems to the governing case

  1. Five pressure systemseach has its own design pressure
  2. One cause at a timethe API 521 list of credible events
  3. The scenario matrixone governing case per device
  4. Model relief runshow high it goes with the trips off
  5. Blocked outletwhy PSV-112 must pass 60 kg/s

Interactive · pick a pressure system

Five systems, five design pressures

A valve protects one system. Settle-out at 69 barg is fine for B, but twice the 36 barg of A.

API 521 · credible single causes

Each event is studied on its own

Blocked outlet

A valve shuts downstream.

Valve failure

A control valve fails open.

Fire

A pool fire heats a vessel.

Tube rupture

Gas enters the cooler water side.

Utility failure

Air or cooling is lost.

Settle-out

The stopped loop equalises.

Not credited: trips or controls that help, or two independent failures together.

Relieving pressure: set + 10 % (one valve) or set + 21 % (fire).

Interactive · pick a relief device

One ★ per device: its governing case

The ★ is the single cause that needs the largest flow; every other row must also fit that valve.

Interactive · copies of the model, trips off

Only the blocked discharge passes its design pressure

Without PSV-112 the discharge climbs to 180 barg; with trips on, PSHH-112 stops K-100 at 135.9.

Interactive · ESDV-113 shuts at t = 0

With PSV-112, all the production goes to the valve

Before the lift UV-108 recycles; once PSV-112 opens, its flow climbs from 41 to 60 kg/s within a minute.

The governing load of PSV-112

Size on the rated flow, not on the first crossing

Sized on 45.0 kg/s

Flow when 138 barg is first crossed. Orifice L, rated 58.5 kg/s: the discharge reaches ≈ 154 barg.

Sized on 60.26 kg/s

Section-2 design flow. Orifice M, rated 73.8 kg/s: the peak stays at 141.7 barg.

Limit: 110 % of 138 = 151.8 barg.

So each device now has its load; part 2 turns a load into an orifice.

Part 1 · summary

What part 1 settled

  • Each system has its design pressure; a valve protects one system.
  • Study one credible cause at a time; helpful trips are not credited.
  • Blocked outlet governs PSV-112 at the rated flow, 60.26 kg/s.
  • Settle-out (69.4 barg) exceeds system A (36 barg): query EQ-RL-01.

How large must each relief valve be?

From a load to an orifice letter

API 520 Part I · critical gas flow, SI units

The area grows with the load and falls with pressure

$$A=\frac{W}{C\,K_d\,P_1\,K_b\,K_c}\sqrt{\frac{T\,Z}{M}},\qquad C=0.03948\sqrt{k\left(\frac{2}{k+1}\right)^{\frac{k+1}{k-1}}}$$
$C$
gas flow coefficient from $k$
–
$k$
heat-capacity ratio of the gas, 1.258
–
$K_d,\,K_b,\,K_c$
discharge 0.975; back-pressure and rupture-disc factors 1
–
$T,\ Z$
relieving temperature, compressibility
K, –
$M$
molar mass, 22.275
kg/kmol

Here $W$ in kg/h and $P_1$ in kPa a give $A$ in mm².

Worked example · PSV-112, blocked outlet step 1 of 2

Relieving pressure and the flow coefficient

Relieving pressure and coefficient$P_1=P_{set}(1+0.10)+1.013,\qquad C=0.03948\sqrt{k\,(2/(k+1))^{(k+1)/(k-1)}}$
$P_1=138\times1.10+1.013=152.81\ \text{bar a}$set plus 10 % overpressure
$P_b/P_1=1.58/152.81=0.010\le0.553$below the critical ratio: choked flow
$C=0.03948\sqrt{1.258\,(2/2.258)^{8.75}}=0.02604$k = 1.258

Worked example · PSV-112, blocked outlet step 2 of 2

1897 mm² needs an M orifice

API 520 area$A=\dfrac{W}{C\,K_d\,P_1\,K_b\,K_c}\sqrt{TZ/M}$
$Z=0.806$ at $T=318.15\ \text{K}$model compressibility at 45 °C
$A=\dfrac{216\,936}{0.02604\times0.975\times15\,281}\sqrt{\dfrac{318.15\times0.806}{22.275}}=1897\ \text{mm}^2$W = 60.26 kg/s × 3600
$A_o=2323\ \text{mm}^2\ (\text{M}),\quad W_r=73.8\ \text{kg/s}$next API 526 letter

Next, the same equation for all five devices.

Interactive · presets from the relief load basis

The load picks the letter

PSV-112 sized on 45 kg/s drops to L, rated 58.5 kg/s: less than the 60.9 kg/s it must pass.

Interactive · API 520 Part II, at the rated flow

Long tail pipes push the valve towards bellows

Built-up back pressure above 10 % of set needs a balanced-bellows valve; inlet loss must stay under 3 %.

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • API 520 turns each load into an area, then an API 526 letter.
  • Orifices: PSV-001 Q, PSV-107 E, PSV-112 M, E-101 L, E-102 N.
  • Back pressure above 10 % of set calls for balanced bellows.
  • Fire is small for gas scrubbers; tube rupture needs CM-side relief.

Part 3 · Blowdown and flare

How fast does K-100 empty, and can the flare header take it?

Part 3 · the plan

From blowdown to the flare header size

  1. The blowdown target6.9 barg in about 15 min
  2. The ESD-2 runpressure, cold gas, flare load
  3. Why V-101 rises firsta fail-open recycle valve
  4. The largest single contingencyair failure, 104.8 kg/s
  5. Mach in the headerDN500 or DN600

API 521 · depressuring guideline

Empty the plant before a fire weakens the steel

Target

6.9 barg or half of DP, whichever is lower, in about 15 min.

How

ESD-2 opens BDV-101 and BDV-112 through 45 mm RO; XV-001 shuts the wells.

Limit

Expanding gas cools: stay above the MDMT, −46 °C.

Now run ESD-2 on a copy of the model and check all three.

Interactive · model run "ESD-2 blowdown"

All three sections reach 6.9 barg in about 6 min

6.9 barg at 365–370 s, coldest gas −22.1 °C, peak flare 84.1 kg/s: inside all three limits.

ESD-2, the first minute

V-101 goes up before it comes down

UV-103 opens

It fails open and returns interstage gas at 60 barg to V-101.

BDV-101 is slower

Its 45 mm RO removes gas more slowly than it arrives.

41.9 barg at 42 s

Above the 36 barg of system A.

Second reason, after settle-out, to rate the suction side 80 barg (EQ-RL-01).

Flare header DN500-FL-100 · at the battery limit

Interactive · seven contingencies

One cause can open many valves at once

Air failure sends every fail-open valve and both BDVs to flare: 104.8 kg/s, the design case.

Interactive · flare load, header size, gas temperature

DN500 runs at Mach 0.72 on air failure

Header$P_{fl}=1.25+2(W/150)^2,\ \ \text{Ma}=v/a$

DN600 drops Mach to 0.50; the alternative is a smaller coincident load (EQ-RL-03).

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • ESD-2 reaches 6.9 barg in about 6 min, well inside 15 min.
  • The coldest gas, −22.1 °C, stays above the −46 °C MDMT.
  • V-101 first rises to 41.9 barg through the open UV-103.
  • Air failure, 104.8 kg/s, sizes the header: DN500 is marginal.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

Study one credible cause at a time, with helpful trips switched off.

2

Size a valve on the flow it must finally pass, not the first crossing.

3

Check inlet loss and back pressure before choosing the valve type.

4

Protect gas-filled vessels from fire by blowdown, inside 15 min.

5

Size the flare header on the largest single contingency.
